- For \(I\): The inner diamond has area \(\frac12\). The upright square joins the midpoints of the diamond’s sides, so its area is half the diamond’s area, namely \(\frac14\). Thus
  \[
  S_I=\frac12-\frac14=\frac14.
  \]

- For \(II\): The shaded triangle has vertices \((0,0)\), \(\left(\frac12,1\right)\), and \(\left(1,\frac12\right)\). Its area is
  \[
  S_{II}=\frac12\left|\frac12\cdot\frac12-1\cdot1\right|=\frac38.
  \]

- For \(III\): The shaded triangle has base equal to the full side length \(1\) and height \(1\), so
  \[
  S_{III}=\frac12\cdot1\cdot1=\frac12.
  \]

Since

\frac14=\frac28<\frac38<\frac48=\frac12,
